references.text: After the resurrection, Jesus eats fish again with the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. In John 21:9-13, the risen Jesus prepares fish and bread for the disciples, confirming his physical reality after the resurrection, just as he ate grilled fish in Luke 24:42.
Earlier in the same chapter, Jesus breaks bread with the travelers to Emmaus in Luke 24:30-31. The meal is a recurring sign of Jesus' physical presence and fellowship after the resurrection.

Peter testifies in Acts 10:41 that the chosen witnesses "ate and drank together with him after he had risen from the dead". This confirms the historical significance of Jesus eating fish with the disciples as proof of his bodily resurrection.

The context immediately before in Luke 24:36-39 shows that Jesus invites the disciples to touch him to see that he is not a spirit, but has flesh and bones. That he then eats grilled fish further emphasizes his physical, bodily resurrection.
In Acts 1:4, it is told that Jesus ate with the apostles (gr. συναλιζόμενος). This connects to the meal in Luke 24:42 as part of Jesus' repeated fellowship with the disciples after the resurrection.
